CHAPTER 14

Career Management
职业管理

The only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven’t found it yet, keep looking. Don’t settle.
——Steve Jobs

做出卓越工作的唯一途径，就是热爱你所做的事。如果你还没找到它，继续找。不要将就。
——Steve Jobs

When you begin your career as a software engineer, the path might seem pretty straightforward: learn to code, get better at coding, and keep coding. As you grow in your career, you’ll find that tech offers many paths forward, combining technical skills, creativity, and opportunities for growth.

当你开始软件工程师的职业生涯时，这条路看起来也许相当直截了当：学写代码，把代码写得更好，然后继续写代码。随着职业发展，你会发现技术行业提供了许多前进的道路，它们结合了技术技能、创造力和成长机会。

In the first section of this chapter, you’ll learn how to plan your career path. This is all about finding out what you’re passionate about, which can lead to a long and satisfying career. Once you discover what you’re interested in, it’s important to know the options available to you.

在本章第一节，你将学习如何规划自己的职业道路。这一切的核心是找到你的热情所在，而它能带你走过一段漫长而令人满足的职业生涯。一旦发现自己的兴趣所在，了解有哪些选择对你来说就很重要。

In the second section of this chapter, you will learn some practical tips and tricks you can use while walking your career path. You’ll discover strategies for documenting your accomplishments, overcoming imposter syndrome, building a professional network, and mastering the interview process to advance your career.

在本章第二节，你将学到一些在职业道路上可以用得上的实用技巧和窍门。你会发现记录成就、克服冒名顶替综合征、建立职业人脉、以及精通面试流程以推进职业发展的策略。

While seeing so many possibilities may feel overwhelming at first, this chapter will help you navigate your journey and make the most of your career. You need to take ownership of your path and make deliberate decisions about where you want to go.

尽管一开始看到这么多可能性可能会让你觉得无所适从，但本章会帮你走好这段旅程，充分利用你的职业生涯。你需要对自己的道路负起责任，审慎地决定自己想去的方向。

Plan Your Career Path

You might find yourself deeply passionate about coding early in your career, and that’s excellent. Later on, your interests may shift; it’s important to recognize that interests and goals can evolve over time.

在职业生涯早期，你可能会发现自己对编程充满热情，这非常好。往后，你的兴趣可能会转移；重要的是要认识到，兴趣和目标会随时间演变。

This chapter begins by helping you develop a career plan. We’ll start with the crucial first step: discovering your passions and identifying your core interests. This foundation will guide you toward a career path that remains both fulfilling and sustainable.

本章从帮你制定职业规划开始。我们将从关键的第一步起步：发现你的热情所在，识别你的核心兴趣。这个基础会指引你走上一条既令人满足又可持续的职业道路。

Next, we’ll explore various career opportunities you might not have considered before. After you’ve identified your passion and chosen a career direction, we’ll discuss how to make strategic decisions to advance along your chosen path.

接下来，我们会探讨你此前可能从未考虑过的各种职业机会。在你找到热情、选定方向之后，我们会讨论如何做出战略性决策，沿所选道路前进。

Find What You’re Passionate About

Every developer has a unique combination of skills, interests, and values that will shape their career. While writing code serves as the foundation for your technical career, discovering what gets you excited about coding will help build a fulfilling and sustainable career path. (For more strategies on identifying and nurturing your interests, see “Let Your Passion Guide You” on page 279.)

每个开发者都有一套独特的技能、兴趣和价值观组合，它们将塑造你的职业生涯。写代码是你技术生涯的基础，而发现是什么让你对编程感到兴奋，则会帮你建起一条令人满足且可持续的职业道路。（关于识别和培养兴趣的更多策略，见第 279 页“让热情指引你”。）

Exploring different domains and technologies

You might have already found a technology or domain that you’re interested in, but if you haven’t, the world of software development encompasses countless business domains and technologies. Early in your career, try working across different areas to discover what truly excites you. Here are some possible project types to explore:

你也许已经找到了自己感兴趣的技术或领域；如果还没有，软件开发的世界包含着无数业务领域和技术。在职业生涯早期，试着在不同领域间工作，去发现什么真正让你兴奋。以下是一些可以探索的项目类型：

  • Consumer applications that millions of people use daily数百万人日常使用的消费级应用
  • Enterprise systems that power businesses支撑企业运转的企业级系统
  • Data-intensive applications for analytics and insights用于分析和洞察的数据密集型应用
  • Infrastructure and DevOps that keep systems running保障系统运行的基础设施与 DevOps
  • Gaming and interactive experiences游戏与交互式体验
  • Educational technology that helps people learn帮助人们学习的教育科技
  • Healthcare systems that improve patient outcomes改善患者诊疗结果的医疗系统
  • Ecommerce platforms that connect buyers and sellers连接买卖双方的电商平台
  • Mobile application development移动应用开发
  • Artificial intelligence and machine learning systems人工智能与机器学习系统

Each domain can present different challenges, impacts, and cultures. For instance, if you find satisfaction in impacting customers, consumer applications might be your calling. If you have always loved video games and have longed to create your own, gaming and interactive experiences might be your path.

每个领域都会呈现不同的挑战、影响和文化。例如，如果你从影响用户中获得满足感，消费级应用也许就是你的使命所在。如果你一直热爱电子游戏、渴望做出自己的游戏，游戏与交互式体验也许就是你的道路。

If you don’t know which technologies or domains you’re interested in, the only way you are going to find out is by experimenting with different ones.

如果你还不知道自己对哪些技术或领域感兴趣，唯一的发现方式就是去尝试不同的东西。

原书第 330 页

Experiment with side projects

If you’re early in your career, chances are you could be limited to the types of projects you’re working on. You might be working in the same domain with the same technologies every day, and you’re not getting exposed to different things.

如果你处于职业生涯早期，你很可能受限于手头项目的类型。你也许每天都在同一个领域、用同一套技术工作，接触不到不同的东西。

Side projects offer a low-risk environment to explore technologies and domains that might be of interest to you. Unlike your day job, you have complete freedom to choose what to build and how to build it. If you’re primarily a backend developer and interested in frontend work, take on something that requires you to build a good-looking frontend.

副项目（side project）提供了一个低风险的环境，让你去探索可能感兴趣的技术和领域。与日常工作不同，你可以完全自由地选择做什么、怎么做。如果你主要是后端开发者却对前端感兴趣，就接一个需要你做漂亮前端的项目。

When selecting what to build with, consider looking at job postings from 10 companies you’d like to work for. Identify the technologies that appear repeatedly across these listings. These are clearly in demand and worth investing your time in. However, don’t limit yourself only to what’s currently popular. Consider deliberately choosing technologies different from your day job. A different programming language, development environment, or platform can challenge you and provide real growth as a software engineer. This approach expands your mental map of how software works and gives you more opportunities to discover what excites you.

在选择用什么来做时，可以看看 10 家你想去的公司的招聘启事。找出在这些启事里反复出现的技术。这些技术显然有需求，值得你投入时间。不过，别把自己只局限在当前流行的东西上。有意识地选一些和日常工作不同的技术。一门不同的编程语言、开发环境或平台，能挑战你，让你作为软件工程师获得真正的成长。这种做法会扩展你对软件如何运作的心智地图，也给你更多机会去发现什么让你兴奋。

Working on personal side projects or contributing to open source is an excellent way to stand out on your resume. While not required, these activities can significantly differentiate you from other candidates when applying for positions internally or at other companies.

做个人副项目或为开源做贡献，是让你简历脱颖而出的绝佳方式。虽然不是硬性要求，但在内部竞聘或申请其他公司职位时，这些活动能让你明显区别于其他候选人。

As you experiment, pay attention to which aspects energize you versus which feel draining. Here’s what to track while coding:

在尝试的过程中，留意哪些方面让你充满能量，哪些又让你感到耗竭。写代码时可以记录以下这些：

  • Which types of problems get you excited to solve?哪类问题让你兴奋地想去解决？
  • Do you prefer building user interfaces or working with data and algorithms?你更喜欢做用户界面，还是和数据、算法打交道？
  • Does debugging complex systems energize you or frustrate you?调试复杂系统是让你充满能量，还是让你沮丧？
  • Do you enjoy the creative aspects of design or the logical precision of backend systems?你享受设计的创造性，还是后端系统的逻辑严谨？

Keep a simple journal noting +1 (energizing) or –1 (draining) for different coding activities, along with a brief note about why. Look for patterns: you might discover that pixel-perfect CSS alignment isn’t for you, or you might find that building interactive web experiences is exactly what excites you about programming.

记一本简单的日志，给不同的编码活动标注 +1（充满能量）或 –1（耗竭），并简短写下原因。寻找其中的模式：你可能会发现像素级对齐的 CSS 并不适合你，也可能发现构建交互式网页体验正是编程让你兴奋之处。

Side Projects That Solve Your Own Problems
解决自己问题的副项目

Dan here. When working on a side project, it’s helpful to build something that is useful to you or solves your own problem. I have had a personal website for as long as I can remember. This allows me to have my own little corner of the internet and show off the things I am working on. I started a blog so that I could get involved with open source projects and teach what I learned back to the community. The point is, I really enjoy working on this, and this has exposed me to frameworks and tools that I would have never used in my day job.
我是 Dan。做副项目时，做一个对你有用、或能解决你自己问题的东西会很有帮助。从我记事起，我就一直有个人网站。这让我在互联网上有了自己的小角落，可以展示我正在做的东西。我开了个博客，好参与开源项目，并把学到的东西教回给社区。关键在于，我真的很享受做这些，而这也让我接触到了日常工作中永远不会用到的框架和工具。

Exploring Your Career Options

Early on in your career, you’re so focused on learning your craft that it’s hard to see the forest for the trees. You’re learning the fundamentals of software development to land that first job or improving for that highly coveted promotion. As far as you know, writing code and getting better at what you do will be your entire career.

在职业生涯早期，你太专注于打磨手艺，以至于只见树木不见森林。你在学习软件开发基础，为的是拿到第一份工作，或为那次梦寐以求的晋升而精进。在你看来，写代码并把它越做越好，就是你整个职业生涯的全部。

What you might not have been told is that software development encompasses diverse career trajectories that go far beyond just writing code. The key to a fulfilling career is being flexible and open to opportunities while maintaining a general direction that aligns with your interests and strengths.

也许没人告诉过你：软件开发包含着远比“写代码”丰富得多的多样职业轨迹。一段令人满足的职业，关键在于保持灵活、对机会开放，同时维持一个与你兴趣和优势相符的大方向。

In this section, you’ll explore paths you can take, from being a technical expert, to leadership, to some alternative paths that are available. It’s all about knowing what options are out there so you can start making decisions now to get on the right path.

在本节，你将探索可以走的道路：从技术专家，到领导力，再到一些可选的替代路径。重点是了解外面有哪些选择，好让你现在就开始做决定，走上正确的道路。

What’s Permanent, What’s Not
什么是永久的，什么不是

Only two career decisions are truly permanent: serious ethical violations or burning bridges with colleagues. Everything else can be changed. Technologies, companies, and even career paths can all be redirected with proper planning and effort.
职业生涯中只有两个决定是真正永久的：严重违反职业道德，以及和同事把关系彻底搞僵。其他一切都可以改变。技术、公司，甚至职业道路，通过恰当的规划和努力都能重新定向。

Technical expert path

The technical expert path (also called the individual contributor or IC track) offers developers a way to advance their careers while remaining hands-on with technology rather than transitioning into management. This track rewards deep technical knowledge, system design skills, and technical leadership. Companies typically organize these roles into ladders that progress from senior engineer through staff, principal, and sometimes distinguished or fellow engineer levels, though titles and structures vary across organizations:

技术专家道路（也叫个人贡献者，即 IC 通道）为开发者提供了一条在不转管理的情况下、继续亲手做技术而晋升的路径。这条通道奖励深厚的技术知识、系统设计能力和技术领导力。公司通常把这些角色组织成职级阶梯，从高级工程师一路到 staff、principal，有时还有 distinguished 或 fellow 工程师等级别，不过各公司的头衔和结构不尽相同：

原书第 332 页

Architect

Software architects design the overall structure of systems and make high-level technical decisions that shape entire projects or organizations. They translate business requirements into technical solutions while establishing standards that guide development teams. Despite their high-level focus, effective architects stay hands-on with code to ensure that their designs are practical and to maintain credibility with development teams. Technical architects do the following:

软件架构师设计系统的整体结构，做出影响整个项目乃至整个组织的高层技术决策。他们把业务需求转化为技术方案，同时建立指导开发团队的标准。尽管关注层面很高，高效的架构师仍会亲自动手写代码，以确保设计切实可行，并在开发团队中保持公信力。技术架构师的职责包括：

  • Design system architectures and make critical technology decisions设计系统架构并做出关键技术决策
  • Balance technical trade-offs while considering business needs在考虑业务需求的同时权衡技术取舍
  • Need strong communication skills to explain technical concepts to nontechnical stakeholders需要很强的沟通能力，向非技术干系人解释技术概念
  • Maintain curiosity and hunger for learning to stay current with evolving technologies保持好奇心和求知欲，跟上不断演进的技术
  • Usually have 8+ years of development experience通常有 8 年以上开发经验

Staff engineer

Staff engineers are senior technical leaders who combine coding with broader influence. They solve complex problems while guiding technical direction beyond their immediate team. This path is for developers who want to stay hands-on with code while having broader impact:

Staff 工程师是资深技术领导者，把写代码与更广泛的影响力结合起来。他们解决复杂问题，同时指导超出本团队范围的技术方向。这条道路适合那些想继续亲手写代码、又希望拥有更广泛影响力的开发者：

  • Focus on technical excellence and engineering best practices专注于技术卓越和工程最佳实践
  • Mentor other developers and influence technical decisions指导其他开发者，并影响技术决策
  • Often work across multiple teams or projects常常跨多个团队或项目工作
  • Typically need deep technical expertise in specific domains通常需要在特定领域拥有深厚技术专长
  • Can match or exceed management compensation at senior levels在高级别可以匹敌甚至超过管理岗薪酬
  • Potential titles could be senior developer, technical lead, principal engineer, or staff engineer可能的头衔包括高级开发、技术负责人、principal 工程师或 staff 工程师

These technical career paths offer developers fulfilling alternatives to management roles, allowing you to grow your impact and compensation while continuing to solve challenging technical problems that you love.

这些技术职业道路为开发者提供了管理岗之外、令人满足的替代选择，让你在继续解决自己热爱的挑战性技术问题的同时，扩大影响力、提升薪酬。

Leadership path

The leadership path offers developers opportunities to guide teams, shape product direction, and drive organizational success. This track rewards strategic thinking, interpersonal skills, and the ability to align technical work with business objectives. Companies typically structure these roles into management hierarchies that progress from team lead to director, VP, and C-level positions, with variations across organizations:

领导力道路为开发者提供了带领团队、塑造产品方向、推动组织成功的机会。这条通道奖励战略思维、人际能力，以及把技术工作与业务目标对齐的能力。公司通常把这些角色组织成管理层级，从团队负责人一路到总监、VP、以及 C 级职位，各公司之间有所差异：

Engineering manager

Engineering managers lead development teams by focusing on people, processes, and delivery. They build effective teams, remove obstacles, and align technical work with business goals while supporting individual growth. Management isn’t for everyone, but it’s a valuable path for those interested in people and process:

工程经理通过关注人、流程和交付来带领开发团队。他们组建高效的团队、扫除障碍，把技术工作与业务目标对齐，同时支持个人成长。管理并不适合所有人，但对那些对人和流程感兴趣的人来说，这是一条有价值的道路：

原书第 333 页
  • Focus on team building, career development, and project delivery专注于团队建设、职业发展和项目交付
  • Require strong interpersonal and organizational skills需要很强的人际与组织能力
  • Often maintain technical knowledge but write little to no code通常保留技术知识，但几乎不写代码
  • Need to balance team happiness with business objectives需要在团队幸福感与业务目标之间取得平衡
  • Compensation often includes significant bonus and equity components薪酬通常包含可观的奖金和股权部分

Technical product manager

Technical product managers bridge the gap between business needs and technical implementation. They define product vision, prioritize features, and collaborate with both technical teams and business stakeholders to deliver valuable solutions. For developers who enjoy bridging business and technology:

技术产品经理弥合业务需求与技术实现之间的鸿沟。他们定义产品愿景、排定功能优先级，并与技术团队和业务干系人协作，交付有价值的方案。适合那些喜欢连接业务与技术的开发者：

  • Transform business requirements into technical solutions把业务需求转化为技术方案
  • Work closely with stakeholders across the organization与全组织的干系人紧密合作
  • Require both technical understanding and business acumen既需要技术理解，也需要商业敏锐度
  • Often do less coding but more strategic thinking通常写代码更少，但战略思考更多
  • Can lead to senior product or strategy roles可通向高级产品或战略岗位

These leadership paths allow technically minded professionals to leverage their experience while developing new skills in people management, strategic thinking, and business alignment.

这些领导力道路让有技术背景的专业人士能利用自己的经验，同时在人员管理、战略思考和业务对齐方面发展新技能。

Alternative paths

Beyond the traditional technical expert and leadership tracks, software engineers can pursue innovative careers that combine technical expertise with other disciplines. These alternative paths often leverage your coding knowledge while developing complementary skills in communication, education, business, or specialized domains. As technology continues to evolve, these hybrid roles frequently offer exciting opportunities to make unique contributions to the tech ecosystem:

除了传统的技术专家和领导力通道，软件工程师还可以追求把技术专长与其他学科结合起来的创新职业。这些替代道路常常利用你的编程知识，同时在沟通、教育、商业或专业领域发展互补技能。随着技术不断演进，这些复合型角色往往提供激动人心的机会，让你对技术生态做出独特贡献：

Developer advocate

Developer advocates serve as a bridge between companies and their technical communities. They help users understand and adopt technologies while bridging community feedback into product teams. This newer path combines technical skills with community engagement:

开发者布道者充当公司与其技术社区之间的桥梁。他们帮助用户理解和采用技术，同时把社区反馈传递给产品团队。这条较新的道路把技术技能与社区运营结合起来：

  • Create content, give talks, and build developer communities创作内容、发表演讲、建设开发者社区
  • Require strong communication and teaching skills需要很强的沟通和教学能力
  • Often travel and perform public speaking常常出差并进行公开演讲
原书第 334 页
  • Need to stay current with technology trends需要跟上技术趋势
  • Can lead to developer relations or technical marketing roles可通向开发者关系或技术营销岗位

Sales engineers

Sales engineers combine deep technical knowledge with a passion to help customers find the right solutions to their problems. They serve as technical experts during the sales process by demonstrating products, addressing technical concerns, and building trust with prospective customers. For developers who enjoy explaining technology and working with people:

销售工程师把深厚的技术知识与帮助客户找到合适解决方案的热情结合起来。他们在销售过程中充当技术专家，演示产品、解答技术顾虑、与潜在客户建立信任。适合那些喜欢讲解技术、和人打交道的开发者：

  • Bridge technical capabilities with business value for customers为客户把技术能力与业务价值连接起来
  • Require strong presentation and interpersonal skills alongside technical expertise除技术专长外，还需要很强的演示和人际能力
  • Often travel to client sites and trade shows常去客户现场和行业展会
  • Need the ability to understand and articulate complex technical concepts to varied audiences需要能向不同受众理解并讲清复杂技术概念
  • Can lead to senior sales roles, technical sales management, or customer success positions可通向高级销售、技术销售管理或客户成功岗位

Technical entrepreneur

Technical entrepreneurs leverage their engineering expertise to build products and businesses from the ground up. They identify market opportunities, develop solutions, and navigate the challenges of creating sustainable ventures. For those interested in building their own ventures:

技术创业者利用自己的工程专长，从零开始打造产品和业务。他们识别市场机会、开发方案，并驾驭创立可持续企业过程中的种种挑战。适合那些有兴趣创办自己事业的人：

  • Combine technical skills with business development把技术技能与业务拓展结合起来
  • Higher risk but potential for significant rewards风险更高，但潜在回报丰厚
  • Require broad knowledge across technology and business需要跨技术与商业的广博知识
  • Often start as side projects while maintaining regular jobs常常在保留正职的同时以副项目起步
  • Can lead to founding successful companies or joining startups early可通向创立成功公司或早期加入创业公司

Developer advocate, sales engineer, and technical entrepreneur aren’t the only alternative paths for software engineers. There are many possible career paths such as site reliability engineer, Development and Operations (DevOps), and more. Remember that, as we mentioned at the beginning of this section, being flexible and open to opportunities throughout your career while maintaining a general direction is essential for growth.

开发者布道者、销售工程师和技术创业者并不是软件工程师仅有的替代道路。还有许多可能的职业道路，比如站点可靠性工程师、研发运维（DevOps）等等。记住，正如本节开头所说，在整个职业生涯中保持灵活、对机会开放，同时维持一个大方向，对成长至关重要。

Talk to people who work in the spaces you’re interested in exploring. Ask them for guidance;1 many people are happy to mentor others. Mention your interests to your manager; if they don’t know what you want, they can’t help you get it. Many companies will provide opportunities to formally or informally shadow people or to even spend a period of time working in a different area. Don’t be afraid to advocate for yourself, as you are responsible for your career progression!

去和那些在你感兴趣领域工作的人聊聊。向他们请教；1很多人很乐意指导别人。把你的兴趣告诉你的经理；如果他们不知道你想要什么，就没法帮你得到它。许多公司会提供正式或非正式的跟岗机会，甚至让你在另一个领域工作一段时间。别不好意思为自己争取，因为职业发展是你自己的责任！

请人喝杯咖啡或吃顿午饭，可能会提高你成功的几率。

Walking Backward from Your Goals

As a software engineer, you’ve developed a valuable skill that allows you to break complex problems into smaller, manageable pieces. This approach allows you to tackle challenges that would be overwhelming if viewed as a single problem statement. The same principle applies to career development.

作为软件工程师，你已经练就了一项宝贵技能：把复杂问题拆解成更小、可管理的小块。这种方法让你能够应对那些如果当成一个整体难题就会让人无从下手的挑战。同样的原则也适用于职业发展。

An effective way to achieve career aspirations is to work backward from your long-term vision by breaking it into smaller, achievable milestones. Think about where you want to be in three to five years. Do you see yourself as a technical architect designing complex systems? As an engineering manager overseeing a team of developers? Working with clients to set the direction of a product? Whatever your path, identifying the intermediate steps will help you get there systematically.

实现职业抱负的一个有效方法，是从你的长期愿景往回倒推，把它拆成更小、可实现的里程碑。想想三到五年后你想成为什么样。你想成为设计复杂系统的技术架构师吗？成为管理一支开发者团队的工程经理吗？还是和客户一起确定产品方向？无论走哪条路，识别出中间步骤都会帮你系统地抵达目标。

For example, here are some milestones if your goal is to become a technical architect:

例如，如果你的目标是成为技术架构师，下面是一些里程碑：

Year 5+

  • Drive architectural decisions for major projects主导重大项目的架构决策
  • Develop cross-team technical standards制定跨团队的技术标准
  • Build influence beyond your immediate team建立超出本团队的影响力
  • Work on your nontechnical skills such as presenting and leading effective meetings打磨你的非技术技能，比如演讲和高效主持会议

Year 3–5

  • Lead technical projects领导技术项目
  • Mentor junior developers指导初级开发者
  • Gain experience with distributed systems获得分布式系统方面的经验
  • Build expertise in scalability and performance optimization在可扩展性和性能优化方面建立专长
  • Work with your architect to assist with their deliverables where possible与你的架构师合作，在可能的地方协助他交付成果

Year 1–2

  • Master your current tech stack精通你当前的技术栈
  • Take on increasingly complex technical challenges承担越来越复杂的技术挑战
  • Start learning system design principles开始学习系统设计原则
  • Schedule periodic one-on-ones with an architect or two in your organization定期约组织里的一两位架构师一对一交流

Learn from Those Who Went Before
向前辈取经

Connect with people in positions you aspire to reach. If you work with architects, ask them about their journey from junior → senior → architect. Learning from their experiences will help inform your own career decisions.
去联系那些身处你向往职位的人。如果你和架构师共事，问问他们从初级 → 高级 → 架构师的历程。从他们的经历中学习，会帮你做出自己的职业决策。

Deliberate Skill Acquisition

If you enjoy learning, you’ve made an excellent career choice. As a software developer, you’re committing to a lifetime of learning. But here’s the reality: you can’t learn everything. No matter how much you might want to, there simply isn’t enough time.

如果你享受学习，那你选对了职业。作为软件开发者，你就是在承诺终身学习。但现实是：你不可能什么都学。无论你多想学，时间就是不够。

In the previous section, you learned how to create a roadmap for your career. To stay on track, avoid chasing every new technology just because it’s trending. The truth is, many of these trendy tools may not exist in a few years. This behavior is sometimes called resume-driven development, where you learn technologies solely to add them to your resume rather than for meaningful career growth.

上一节你学习了如何为职业制定路线图。为了不走偏，别仅仅因为某样技术正在流行就去追。事实是，这些时髦工具里有很多几年后可能就不存在了。这种行为有时被称为“简历驱动开发”——你学技术只是为了把它写进简历，而不是为了有意义的职业成长。

In Chapter 12, you learned some valuable tips on how to learn. This invaluable skill, combined with deliberate skill acquisition, can help you reach your goals faster. Random learning produces random results. To progress effectively in your career, you need a structured approach to acquiring new skills.

在第 12 章，你学到了一些关于如何学习的宝贵技巧。这项宝贵技能加上刻意的技能习得，能帮你更快达成目标。随机学习产生随机结果。要在职业生涯中有效进步，你需要一套结构化的方法来获得新技能。

To help with deliberate skill acquisition, you can build a strong foundation of the fundamentals, develop your expertise in the shape of a T, and focus on strategic learning.

为了帮助刻意习得技能，你可以：打下扎实的基础、把专长发展成 T 字形、并专注于战略性学习。

Core skills

Core skills form the bedrock of your technical expertise and remain valuable regardless of changing technology trends. These skills represent the foundation, the vertical bar of your T-shaped expertise. Building a strong foundation is essential before adding complexity. Focus first on mastering these fundamentals of software engineering:

核心技能是你技术专长的基石，无论技术潮流如何变化都始终有价值。这些技能代表基础，也就是你 T 字形专长里那一竖。在叠加复杂性之前，打下坚实基础至关重要。首先专注于掌握软件工程的这些基本功：

  • Data structures and algorithms数据结构与算法
  • Design patterns设计模式
  • Testing methodologies测试方法论
  • Version control版本控制
  • Database design数据库设计
原书第 337 页

T-shaped development

Once you have developed a solid foundation, you can expand your expertise. T-shaped development creates a powerful combination of depth and breadth that makes you both specialized and adaptable in an industry that is constantly evolving:

一旦打下扎实基础，你就可以扩展专长。T 字形发展把深度和广度有力地结合起来，让你在一个不断演进的行业里既专业又能适应：

  • The vertical bar represents deep knowledge in your primary technology stack.竖线代表你在主力技术栈上的深厚知识。
  • The horizontal bar represents broader knowledge across related technologies.横线代表你在相关技术上的更广博的知识。

For example, if you’re a backend Java developer:

例如，如果你是后端 Java 开发者：

  • Deep knowledge: Java, Spring Framework, data storage (SQL/NoSQL)深度知识：Java、Spring Framework、数据存储（SQL/NoSQL）
  • Broad knowledge: Basic frontend skills, DevOps practices, system design广度知识：基础前端技能、DevOps 实践、系统设计

Strategic learning

Before investing your limited time in acquiring new skills, evaluate each opportunity against these critical criteria:

在投入有限时间学习新技能之前，用以下这些关键标准评估每个机会：

  • Does this align with your career goals?这与你的职业目标一致吗？
  • Is this technology/skill likely to be relevant in three to five years?这项技术/技能在三到五年后还有用吗？
  • Will this knowledge give you a competitive advantage?这些知识会给你带来竞争优势吗？
  • Will this make you more valuable in your current role or team?这会让你在当前岗位或团队里更有价值吗？
  • Does this new thing excite you?这个新东西让你兴奋吗？

Deliberate skill acquisition transforms your learning from random to strategic. By focusing on core skills first, developing T-shaped expertise, and evaluating learning opportunities against your career goals, you’ll make better decisions about where to invest your time. This targeted approach not only accelerates your growth but also ensures that you develop mastery in the areas that truly matter to your unique career journey.

刻意的技能习得把你的学习从随机变为有战略。通过先专注核心技能、发展 T 字形专长、并对照职业目标评估学习机会，你会在“时间投在哪里”上做出更好的决策。这种有针对性的方法不仅加速你的成长，也确保你在对你独特职业道路真正重要的领域培养出精通。

Build a personal technology radar

Now that you understand the importance of deliberate skill acquisition, it’s time to put it into action by learning about technology radar. A technology radar is a decision-making and communication tool that helps organizations track and categorize emerging technologies, tools, frameworks, platforms, and techniques over time.

既然你理解了刻意技能习得的重要性，是时候行动起来，了解一下技术雷达（technology radar）了。技术雷达是一种决策与沟通工具，帮助组织随时间追踪并分类新兴技术、工具、框架、平台和方法。

原书第 338 页

It’s especially valuable for software development teams, product innovators, and technology leaders. Originally developed for organizations by Thoughtworks, you can adapt this concept for personal use.

它对软件开发团队、产品创新者和技术领导者尤其有价值。技术雷达最初由 Thoughtworks 为企业开发，你可以把这个概念改造为个人所用。

Your radar should have four quadrants:

你的雷达应有四个象限：

  1. Language & Frameworks语言与框架
  2. Tools & Infrastructure工具与基础设施
  3. Platforms & APIs平台与 API
  4. Techniques & Methodologies技术与方法论

Within each quadrant, categorize technologies into rings:

在每个象限内，把技术归入不同的环：

Adopt

Technologies you’re currently using and mastering.

你当前正在使用并精通的技术。

Trial

Technologies you’re actively learning or experimenting with.

你正在积极学习或实验的技术。

Assess

Technologies you’re researching but haven’t started learning.

你在调研但还没开始学的技术。

Hold

Technologies you’ve decided not to pursue right now.

你已决定暂不跟进的技术。

Creating your first technology radar might seem overwhelming, but beginning with what you know provides solid footing. Start by mapping your current technical landscape and gradually expand outward. You could create this by doing something as simple as writing it on a piece of paper all the way up to using a tool from Thoughtworks called Build Your Own Radar, or BYOR. Whatever works for you and your team, the important thing is capturing your technology ecosystem in a way that sparks meaningful discussion and guides future decisions:

创建你的第一个技术雷达也许看起来让人望而生畏，但从你已知的东西入手就能站稳脚跟。先画出你当前的技术版图，再逐步向外扩展。你可以简单到写在一张纸上，也可以用 Thoughtworks 的工具 Build Your Own Radar（简称 BYOR）。无论用什么适合你和团队的方式，重要的是以一种能引发有意义讨论、并指导未来决策的方式，把你的技术生态捕捉下来：

  1. List technologies in your current stack. Include languages, frameworks, and tools you use daily. Note your proficiency level with each and identify any knowledge gaps worth addressing.列出你当前技术栈中的技术。包括你每天用的语言、框架和工具。标注你对每项的熟练程度，找出值得弥补的知识缺口。
  2. Add technologies used in job postings that interest you. Review positions you’d like to have in the next one to two years. What technologies appear frequently in these listings? Which ones are listed as “required” versus “nice-to-have”?加入你感兴趣的招聘启事中用到的技术。回顾你未来一两年想做的职位。这些启事里哪些技术频繁出现？哪些列为“必备”，哪些列为“加分项”？
  3. Include emerging technologies from tech blogs and conferences. Pay attention to solutions gaining traction in your specific domain. Don’t chase every trend, but identify patterns in what industry leaders are adopting.纳入来自技术博客和大会的新兴技术。留意在你特定领域里正获得关注的方案。别追每一个潮流，但要识别行业领导者在采用什么中的模式。
  4. Review and update periodically. Set a quarterly reminder to reassess your radar. Technologies may move between categories as their relevance to your career changes.定期回顾和更新。设一个季度提醒来重新评估你的雷达。随着技术与你职业的相关性变化，它们可能会在类别间移动。
原书第 339 页

Remember
记住

Remember: Your radar should reflect both current popular technologies and future trends. It is a tool to help you focus your attention on what you want to learn in the near and medium term.
记住：你的雷达应同时反映当前流行技术和未来趋势。它是一个帮你把注意力集中在近期和中期想学什么上的工具。

To make this practical, Table 14-1 presents an example of what a junior developer’s technology radar might look like.

Techniques & Methodologies技术与方法论System design patterns系统设计模式Microservices architecture微服务架构

Try to come up with a regular cadence to review and update your radar. Technology moves quickly, and what is relevant today could be obsolete tomorrow. Use your radar in combination with your career roadmap to stay the course. None of these decisions are permanent; you should adapt as your needs and desires change. Your own interests will evolve as well: your passion matters. If you’re not excited about the topic, you’ll never invest your most precious assets: your time and attention.

尽量定一个固定节奏来回顾和更新你的雷达。技术发展很快，今天还相关的东西明天可能就过时了。把雷达和职业路线图结合起来使用，坚持走下去。这些决定没有一个是永久的；你应随需求和愿望的变化而调整。你自己的兴趣也会演变：你的热情很重要。如果你对某个主题不兴奋，你就永远不会投入你最宝贵的资产：时间和注意力。

Aligning Career Choices with Life Phases

Your career decisions won’t happen in a vacuum. They are deeply influenced by your current life phase and personal circumstances. Everyone’s story on why they got into software development and how they got to where they are today is unique. What might have made sense as a career path right out of school might not be the same later in life with young kids at home, let alone as a freshly minted empty nester.

你的职业决策不会发生在真空里。它们深受你当前人生阶段和个人处境的影响。每个人进入软件开发行业的原因、以及如何走到今天的故事都是独一无二的。刚毕业时合理的职业道路，到了上有老下有小的阶段可能就不一样了，更不用说刚成为空巢老人的时候。

Five main factors typically drive career decisions:

通常有五个主要因素驱动职业决策：

Compensation (salary, benefits, equity)

Are you paid adequately for your work?

你的工作得到了足够的报酬吗？

Team and workplace culture

Do you like the people and organization?

你喜欢这里的人和组织吗？

Work content and technical challenges

Do you like the work?

你喜欢这份工作吗？

原书第 340 页

Growth opportunities and future prospects

Will this job help you get the next job? Also consider the opportunity cost: what other experiences, skills, or connections might you miss by choosing this path over alternatives?

这份工作能帮你拿到下一份工作吗？还要考虑机会成本：选择这条路而非其他，你可能错过哪些其他的经历、技能或人脉？

Work–life balance

Does this role allow you to maintain your personal relationships and well-being?

这个岗位能让你维持好个人关系和身心健康吗？

While all of these factors should be taken into consideration, their priority may shift based on your life phase. For instance:

虽然所有这些因素都应考虑，但它们的优先级会随你的人生阶段而变化。例如：

Early career

You might prioritize growth opportunities and challenging work, accepting lower pay to gain experience at a cutting-edge startup.

你可能把成长机会和有挑战的工作放在首位，接受较低的薪酬，去前沿初创公司积累经验。

Family formation

Health insurance, stable hours, and predictable income might become crucial, making established companies more attractive.

医保、稳定的工时和可预期的收入可能变得至关重要，让成熟公司更有吸引力。

Mid-career

With experience under your belt, you might focus on maximizing compensation through strategic moves between companies.

有了经验积累，你可能专注于通过在公司间的战略性跳槽来最大化薪酬。

Later career

Work–life balance and team culture often become more important than rapid career advancement. Many experienced developers also find motivation in creating a lasting legacy through mentoring others, contributing to meaningful projects, or building something that will have lasting impact.

工作与生活的平衡、团队文化往往比快速晋升更重要。许多资深开发者还通过指导他人、为有意义的项目做贡献、或打造有持久影响力的东西来创造遗产，从中找到动力。

When aligning your career choices with your life phases, you should consider the type of company you want to work for as well as some practical considerations such as whether you are willing to relocate or travel for work.

在让职业选择与人生阶段对齐时，你应考虑想在哪类公司工作，以及一些实际因素，比如你是否愿意为工作搬家或出差。

Company types and their work–life fit

When searching for your next opportunity, it might help to examine the types of companies out there and how they align with your different life phases:

在寻找下一个机会时，不妨看看外面都有哪些类型的公司，以及它们如何与你不同的人生阶段匹配：

Startups

A newly established business focused on developing a novel product or service

新成立的、专注于开发新颖产品或服务的公司

  • Pros: Rapid and diverse learning opportunities, as you’ll likely need to wear many hats and tackle diverse challenges优点：快速而多样的学习机会，因为你很可能需要身兼数职、应对各种挑战
  • Cons: Long hours, high risk of failure, and limited resources or benefits缺点：工时长、失败风险高、资源或福利有限
原书第 341 页

Traditional companies

Companies across various industries (healthcare, finance, retail, manufacturing, etc.) that use technology to support their primary business but aren’t technology companies themselves

各行业（医疗、金融、零售、制造等）中用技术支撑其主业、但本身并非科技公司的企业

  • Pros: Stability, predictable hours, strong benefits packages, good work–life balance优点：稳定、工时可预期、福利丰厚、工作生活平衡好
  • Cons: Typically slower-paced development, less bleeding-edge technology, lower total compensation缺点：通常开发节奏较慢、技术没那么前沿、总薪酬较低

Big tech

Large, influential technology companies such as Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Apple, Meta (Facebook), and Microsoft

大型、有影响力的科技公司，如 Alphabet（Google）、Amazon、Apple、Meta（Facebook）和 Microsoft

  • Pros: Financial security, strong benefits, credibility, cutting-edge technology opportunities优点：财务保障、福利好、公信力强、接触前沿技术的机会
  • Cons: Highly selective hiring process, lengthy interview preparation requiring algorithm study缺点：招聘筛选严格、面试准备周期长，需要刷算法题

Consulting

Companies that provide expert advice and services to other organizations, through consulting firms or as an independent freelancer

通过咨询公司或作为独立自由职业者，向其他组织提供专家建议和服务的公司/角色

  • Pros: Broad experience across multiple companies and technologies, exposure to a variety of industries, often higher compensation. As an independent consultant, you get to pick your own projects and have greater flexibility.优点：跨多家公司、多种技术的广博经验，接触各种行业，薪酬通常更高。作为独立顾问，你可以自己挑项目，灵活性更大。
  • Cons: Requires quick adaptation to new environments and technology stacks, potential travel requirements. Independent consulting adds the challenge of finding your own clients and managing business operations.缺点：需要快速适应新环境和新技术栈，可能要出差。独立咨询还增加了自己找客户、管理业务运营的挑战。

Practical considerations

When evaluating potential job opportunities, it might not come down to just the type of company you want to work for. If all things are considered equal, some of these practical factors might matter more depending on your current phase of life:

评估潜在工作机会时，可能不只是取决于你想去哪类公司。如果其他条件都相当，下面这些实际因素根据你当前的人生阶段可能更重要：

  • Do you need comprehensive health insurance, or can you get it through a partner?你需要一份全面的医保吗，还是可以通过配偶获得？
  • Is geographic stability important to you?地点稳定对你重要吗？
  • Can you handle the financial uncertainty of equity over salary?你能接受用股权替代薪水带来的财务不确定性吗？
  • Do you have the time and energy for an intense learning curve?你有时间和精力应对陡峭的学习曲线吗？
  • Do you want to travel more or less?你想多出差还是少出差？
  • Will this move help you build your own personal brand?这次跳槽会帮你建立个人品牌吗？
原书第 342 页
  • Do you prefer to work from home or in an office? If the latter, is the commute reasonable?你更喜欢居家办公还是去办公室？如果是后者，通勤可接受吗？
  • What is your tolerance for risk?你的风险承受能力如何？
  • Does this opportunity offer you the work–life balance you need?这个机会能给你需要的工作生活平衡吗？
  • Do you like the business domain or product? Are you excited to learn it?你喜欢这个业务领域或产品吗？你有兴趣去了解它吗？

There’s no single right path, just the right choice for your current circumstances. Different company types (startups, big tech, consulting) will align with your changing life phases, while practical considerations like health insurance needs, location stability, and work–life balance preferences will help guide your decision making.

没有唯一正确的道路，只有适合你当前处境的选择。不同公司类型（初创、大厂、咨询）会与你不断变化的人生阶段相匹配，而医保需求、地点稳定、工作生活平衡偏好等实际因素会帮你做出决策。

Also, plan with flexibility. When making career decisions, set ambitious goals but try to build in flexibility for unexpected challenges or changes in your personal life. Your career path rarely unfolds exactly as you planned it, and that is OK. This is often where the most valuable growth and learning happens. Focus on maintaining steady progress over time rather than burning out on an aggressive predetermined timeline.

另外，规划时要留有余地。做职业决策时，定下有抱负的目标，但也要为意外的挑战或个人生活的变化留出弹性。你的职业道路很少完全按计划展开，这没关系。最有价值的成长和学习往往就发生在这里。专注于随时间稳步前进，而不是按一个激进的预定时间表把自己燃尽。

Walking Your Career Path

Now that you understand how to plan your career path, let’s explore practical tips for the journey ahead. As you progress, remember to enjoy each step along the way. We often focus so intently on our destination that we forget to celebrate our current accomplishments. In this section, you’ll learn strategies for documenting your achievements, managing imposter syndrome, building your professional network, and succeeding in interviews.

既然你已了解如何规划职业道路，我们来探索未来旅程中的实用技巧。在前行的过程中，记得享受沿途的每一步。我们常常过于专注于终点，以至于忘记庆祝当下的成就。在本节，你将学习记录成就、管理冒名顶替综合征、建立职业人脉、以及在面试中取得成功的策略。

Celebrate and Record Your Wins

The world of software development moves at a rapid pace. You pour everything into solving one problem before quickly moving on to the next. Whether you’re fixing a complex bug, implementing a new feature, or receiving positive feedback from colleagues or community members, every win matters, no matter how small it seems. Take the time to record these victories, both large and small, as they happen.

软件开发的世界节奏飞快。你倾尽全力解决一个问题，然后又迅速扑向下一个。无论你是在修一个复杂 bug、实现一个新功能，还是从同事或社区成员那里收到正面反馈，每一个胜利都重要，无论它看起来多小。花点时间，在这些胜利发生时把它们记录下来，无论大小。

A “wins document” serves multiple purposes. It acts as a powerful reminder when imposter syndrome (we’ll talk about this later in the chapter) strikes, and it provides a confidence boost during tough times. It’s also a valuable resource for performance reviews, resume updates, and job interviews. Moreover, it helps you track your professional growth and identify patterns in what you’ve considered wins throughout your career.

一份“成就文档”有多种用途。当冒名顶替综合征（本章稍后会谈到）袭来时，它是强有力的提醒；在艰难时期，它能提升信心。它也是绩效评估、更新简历和求职面试时的宝贵素材。此外，它帮你追踪职业成长，识别你整个职业生涯中把什么视为胜利的模式。

To document your wins, find a place where you can keep a running log of your achievements. A digital artifact synced across devices and backed up to the cloud is ideal, but if you prefer writing it down on good old-fashioned paper, go ahead and do that. It doesn’t need to be a standalone knowledge management application or have fancy structure to it; an Apple Note or Google Document can easily be accessed on your phone and laptop. Here are some things you can include in your document:2

要记录成就，找一个地方持续记录你的成绩。跨设备同步、云端备份的数字文档最理想；但如果你更喜欢写在老式纸上，那就写纸上。它不必是一个独立的知识管理应用，也不必有花哨的结构；一个 Apple 备忘录或 Google 文档就能让你在手机和笔记本电脑上方便地访问。你可以在文档里记录这些内容：2

原书第 343 页
  • Technical wins (successfully implemented features, solved bugs)技术上的胜利（成功实现功能、解决 bug）
  • Process improvements you have initiated你发起的流程改进
  • Positive feedback from a colleague, stakeholder, and members of the community来自同事、干系人和社区成员的正面反馈
  • New skills you learned你学到的新技能
  • Presentations or knowledge-sharing sessions you’ve led你主持的演讲或知识分享会
2 Including dates can be extremely helpful for reviews and resume updates.
写上日期对绩效评估和更新简历极有帮助。

Be specific rather than exhaustive when documenting your work; you’ll want to remember the details later. Instead of writing “Improved performance in our flagship application,” write “Improved performance by 25% in our flagship application by enabling virtual threads and improving customer experience.” The second version is much more impactful. Such specific achievements are perfect for your resume when seeking new opportunities, whether within your current company or elsewhere.

记录工作时要具体，而不是面面俱到；你以后会想记得这些细节。别写“改进了我们旗舰应用的性能”，而要写“通过启用虚拟线程、改善客户体验，把旗舰应用的性能提升了 25%”。第二个版本有说服力得多。这样具体的成就，无论在公司内部还是外部寻找新机会时，都是简历上的绝佳素材。

Overcome Imposter Syndrome

Does persistent doubt ever creep into your thoughts and ask questions like, “Do I belong here?” or “Can I really do this?” or “Am I smart enough to do this?” It’s called imposter syndrome, and here’s the truth: those feelings might stick with you throughout your entire career. But here is the good news: that’s completely healthy, and it can actually be a driving force for growth.

那种挥之不去的怀疑是否曾潜入你的脑海，问你这样的问题：“我配待在这里吗？”“我真的能做好吗？”“我够聪明吗？”这叫冒名顶替综合征（imposter syndrome）。真相是：这些感觉可能会伴随你整个职业生涯。但好消息是：这完全正常，而且它实际上可以成为成长的驱动力。

What imposter syndrome really is

As you move through your career, you will one day realize that those initial feelings of imposter syndrome weren’t because you didn’t belong; they were signs that you care about doing good work. Imposter syndrome is also an indication you understand how vast the ocean of things you don’t know actually is. Beware the person who “knows everything.” They don’t, and they can often be dangerous on a project. Software is a specialized field, and you cannot know every detail. It takes humility and confidence. There are things you know, and there are things you don’t know, and that’s perfectly fine.

随着职业生涯推进，有一天你会意识到，最初那些冒名顶替综合征的感觉并不是因为你不配；而是说明你在乎把工作做好。冒名顶替综合征也表明你明白自己不知道的那片海洋有多辽阔。要当心那些“什么都懂”的人。他们并不真懂，而且在项目上往往很危险。软件是一个专业领域，你不可能知道每个细节。这需要谦逊，也需要自信。有你知道的事，也有你不知道的事，这完全没问题。

Here are some common signs of imposter syndrome as a software developer:

作为软件开发者，冒名顶替综合征有一些常见征兆：

  • Hesitating to speak up in technical discussions在技术讨论中不敢发言
  • Feeling like you need to know everything before contributing觉得在做贡献之前必须什么都懂
原书第 344 页
  • Comparing yourself to more experienced developers把自己和更有经验的开发者比较
  • Attributing your successes to luck rather than skill把成功归因于运气而非技能
  • Worrying that others will “discover” you don’t belong担心别人会“发现”你其实不配

These feelings are completely normal. People often feel overwhelmed by the vast amount of knowledge they think they need to possess. The field of software development is enormous,3 and it’s impossible to know everything, and that’s perfectly fine.

这些感觉完全正常。人们常常被自己以为需要掌握的海量知识压得喘不过气。软件开发这个领域极其庞大，3不可能什么都知道，而这完全没关系。

3 You cannot learn it all.
你不可能把它全学完。

How to overcome imposter syndrome

While it’s easy to feel like an imposter, these feelings don’t have to hold you back. In fact, they can be a sign that you’re challenging yourself and striving for improvement. This section focuses on transforming those feelings into a powerful force for positive change.

虽然很容易觉得自己像个冒牌货，但这些感觉不必成为你的阻碍。事实上，它们可以说明你在挑战自己、追求进步。本节专注于把这些感觉转化为积极改变的强大力量。

Using doubt as motivation. Instead of viewing imposter syndrome as purely negative self-doubt, you can transform these feelings into powerful motivation for growth. Don’t see failure as a bad thing but as an opportunity to learn. Yes, there will be bumps along the journey, but that’s OK. Once you stop fearing failure, real growth begins. That doubt about your technical expertise in a language or framework? Use it to fuel your mastery. You can overcome those feelings we saw in the previous section:

把怀疑当作动力。别把冒名顶替综合征纯粹看成消极的自我怀疑，你可以把它转化为成长的强大动力。别把失败看成坏事，而要看成学习的机会。是的，旅途上会有颠簸，但没关系。一旦你不再害怕失败，真正的成长就开始了。那种对自己在某门语言或框架上技术专长的怀疑？用它来点燃你精通的火焰。你可以克服上一节里看到的那些感觉：

Hesitating to speak up in technical discussions

Speak from your experiences. No one can invalidate your personal experience. If you’re wrong, learn from it.

从你的经历出发发言。没有人能否定你的亲身经历。如果你错了，从中学习。

Feeling like you need to know everything before contributing

Accept that you’ll never know everything. The sooner you embrace this, the faster you’ll grow.

接受你永远不可能什么都知道。你越早拥抱这一点，成长就越快。

Comparing yourself to more experienced developers

There will always be someone more knowledgeable—embrace it. Being in their presence is an opportunity to learn.

永远会有比你更懂的人——拥抱这一点。和他们在一起就是学习的机会。

Attributing your successes to luck rather than skill

Luck is preparation meeting opportunity. When you learn from failures and keep improving, your successes come from skill, not chance.

运气是准备遇上机会。当你从失败中学习、持续进步，你的成功就来自技能，而非偶然。

Worrying that others will “discover” you don’t belong

You belong here. The sooner you believe this, the sooner you can enjoy your career. It won’t be easy, but with dedication, you can accomplish anything.

你属于这里。你越早相信这一点，就能越早享受你的职业。这不会容易，但只要投入，你可以成就任何事。

原书第 345 页

Building confidence through action. You gain confidence by encountering the same problem multiple times. The first time you face a challenge, your mind might race with panicked thoughts of “How do I fix this?” while feeling completely lost. When you complete your bug fix or new feature and submit it for code review, welcome the feedback you receive. The reviewers aren’t necessarily smarter than you; they’ve just encountered similar problems more frequently. Consider a lightweight retrospective: what worked, what didn’t, what would you do differently in the future? While it’s important to embrace feedback, you also need to learn to stand firm on decisions you feel strongly about. This demonstrates conviction in your thoughts, not argumentativeness. The next time you encounter this challenge, you’ll draw from your experience and know exactly what to do. Eventually, confidence and experience become one and the same. Like riding a bike, facing the same problem repeatedly makes it second nature. What was once intimidating (like those first wobbly attempts on a bike) becomes effortless.

通过行动建立信心。你通过多次遇到同一个问题来获得信心。第一次面对挑战时，你的脑海里可能惊慌地闪过“这怎么修？”的念头，同时感到完全不知所措。当你修完 bug 或完成新功能、提交代码评审时，欢迎你收到的反馈。评审者未必比你聪明；他们只是更频繁地遇到过类似问题。做一个轻量回顾：什么有效、什么没效、以后你会怎么做 differently？拥抱反馈很重要，但你也需要学会在自己强烈认同的决定上站稳立场。这展现的是你对自己想法的确信，而非好争辩。下次再遇到这个挑战，你会从经验中汲取，确切知道该怎么做。最终，信心和经验会合二为一。就像骑自行车，反复面对同一个问题会让它变成第二天性。曾经让你胆怯的事（比如最初骑在车上摇摇晃晃的尝试）会变得毫不费力。

Recognizing opportunities for growth. When browsing your issue tracker, challenge yourself by picking a complex task. While it’s tempting to grab another ticket similar to your last 10 fixes, that won’t help you grow. Don’t be afraid to pick up an issue from an unfamiliar area of the system. You’ll not only gain broader knowledge of the entire system but also strengthen your problem-solving skills by tackling diverse challenges.

识别成长机会。浏览 issue 跟踪系统时，挑一个复杂的任务来挑战自己。虽然再拿一个和你前 10 次修复类似的工单很诱人，但那不会帮你成长。别害怕从系统不熟悉的领域接一个 issue。你不仅会获得对整个系统更广的知识，还会通过应对多样挑战来强化解决问题的能力。

By taking on issues in parts of the application that other developers avoid, you’ll become more valuable to your team. You’ll establish yourself as the domain expert for “payment systems” or whichever area you master.

通过承担其他开发者回避的那部分应用的 issue，你会对团队更有价值。你会把自己打造成“支付系统”或你精通的任何领域的领域专家。

Remember that imposter syndrome is completely normal and those feelings may persist throughout your career. Use them as a daily driver of force for growth rather than a barrier. Another driver for growth is who you surround yourself with, and in the next section, you’ll learn how to build your professional community.

记住，冒名顶替综合征完全正常，这些感觉可能伴随你整个职业生涯。把它们当作日常的成长动力，而不是障碍。另一个成长动力是你和谁为伍。下一节，你将学习如何建立自己的职业社区。

Build Your Professional Community

Networking is not just for computers. When it comes to career growth, developers often focus solely on technical skills, which are obviously important to your career. However, the personal connections you build throughout your career are just as valuable. Building a professional community isn’t about the number of followers you have on a social network; it’s about the genuine relationships that you build throughout your career. Having people you can reach out to for advice, job opportunities, or to just vent about something that happened on your project is key to your success.

人脉（networking）不只是计算机网络的事。说到职业成长，开发者常常只专注于技术技能——技术技能对职业当然重要。然而，你在整个职业生涯中建立的个人关系同样宝贵。建立职业社区，不在于你在社交网络上有多少粉丝；而在于你在整个职业生涯中建立的真诚关系。有一些你可以寻求建议、寻找工作机会、或仅仅倾诉项目上烦心事的人，是你成功的关键。

If the word “networking” makes you think of crowded conference mixers and forced small talk, you’re not alone. But that’s not what effective networking looks like.

如果“人脉”这个词让你想到拥挤的大会酒会和被迫的寒暄，那你不是一个人。但高效的人脉经营并不是那个样子。

community members. You’re also likely to be more engaged during presentations compared to watching a virtual meeting in the background while multitasking at home.

You can also easily join multiple communities simultaneously, expanding your knowledge across technologies and specializations.

Of course, there are trade-offs to consider. Online interactions often lack the depth and personal connection of face-to-face meetings. It can be harder to form meaningful relationships through text-based communications alone. Additionally, the 24/7 nature of online communities can sometimes lead to information overload or feeling pressured to constantly stay engaged.

当然，也有需要权衡的地方。在线互动往往缺乏面对面交流的深度和人际连接。仅凭文字交流更难形成有意义的关系。此外，在线社区 7×24 小时的特性有时会导致信息过载，或让你感到必须时刻在线的压力。

Regardless of your technology interests, you’ll find numerous online communities covering virtually any language, platform, or specialty. If you can’t find a community that matches your specific interests, many platforms make it simple to create your own space and invite like-minded professionals.

无论你对什么技术感兴趣，你都会找到覆盖几乎任何语言、平台或专业的众多在线社区。如果你找不到匹配你特定兴趣的社区，许多平台都让你能轻松创建自己的空间、邀请志同道合的专业人士。

Cultivating Your Professional Relationships

Building a network through meaningful connections is essential for career growth, but like any relationship, these connections need fostering and nurturing over time. Remember that building a community isn’t about what you can extract from it; this transactional mindset won’t lead to meaningful relationships. Instead, focus on creating mutual value through genuine contribution, and professional growth will naturally follow.

通过有意义的关系建立人脉对职业成长至关重要，但和任何关系一样，这些关系需要长期培育和滋养。记住，建立社区不是关于你能从中索取什么；这种交易型心态不会带来有意义的关系。相反，专注于通过真诚的贡献创造互惠价值，职业成长会自然随之而来。

Professional relationships that last are built on core principles that reflect both your technical expertise and interpersonal skills:

持久的职业关系建立在一些核心原则之上，这些原则同时体现你的技术专长和人际能力：

Authenticity

Be yourself and be genuine in all of your interactions. If you don’t understand a technical concept during a meeting or code review, admit it and use it as a learning opportunity. Your colleagues will appreciate your honesty and be more willing to help out.

真诚。做你自己，在所有交往中保持真诚。如果在会议或代码评审中你没理解某个技术概念，承认它，并把它当作学习机会。你的同事会欣赏你的诚实，也更愿意帮你。

Dependability

Dependability is an important skill across all walks of life. Deliver on your commitments reliably. If you say you’ll have a feature ready for review by Thursday, make it happen. When you can’t meet a deadline, communicate it early. If you regularly meet people in your network for coffee or lunch, show up on time and don’t cancel at the last minute. This dependability builds trust with both team members and individuals in your professional community

可靠。可靠在各行各业都是重要技能。可靠地兑现你的承诺。如果你说周四前会把一个功能准备好评审，那就做到。当你无法按期时，尽早沟通。如果你定期和人脉圈里的人约咖啡或午饭，准时到，别临时取消。这种可靠会在团队成员和职业社区的人之间建立信任。

Mutual value

Don’t just rely on that coworker with strong frontend skills for answers; build a relationship where both of you benefit. Share your knowledge freely while being open to learning from others.

互惠。别遇事就只去找那个前端很强的同事要答案；建立一种双方都受益的关系。自由分享你的知识，同时敞开向他人学习。

Respect

Be open to the possibility that you don’t have all the answers. Acknowledge and value diverse perspectives and experiences. When discussing technical approaches, listen actively to alternative solutions, even if they differ from your preferred method. Remember that in software engineering, there are often multiple valid ways to solve a problem.

尊重。对“你并非什么都知道”这种可能保持开放。承认并重视多样的视角和经验。讨论技术方案时，积极倾听替代方案，即使它们和你偏好的做法不同。记住，在软件工程中，解决一个问题往往有多种有效方式。

Communication

Communication is the foundation of any relationship, and it’s no different when it comes to your professional network. Clear, effective communication is crucial in software development. Whether you’re explaining your code changes,

沟通。沟通是任何关系的基础，职业人脉也不例外。清晰、有效的沟通在软件开发中至关重要。无论你是在解释代码改动、

原书第 349 页

discussing architectural decisions, or providing status updates, strive for clarity and consider your audience’s technical background.

（接上页）讨论架构决策，还是汇报状态，都要力求清晰，并考虑听众的技术背景。

Maintain and engage your network

Building connections is important, but maintaining meaningful relationships with your existing network is equally crucial for long-term career success. This requires ongoing investment of time and energy.

建立联系很重要，但与现有网络维持有意义的关系对长期职业成功同样关键。这需要持续投入时间和精力。

Deliberately engage your communities by sharing your unique perspective and actively participating. Write about problems you’ve solved, contribute to discussions on GitHub or Stack Overflow, and ask thoughtful questions during meetings. Document your solutions: you’ll thank yourself later when you encounter the same problem again. Being a passive observer isn’t enough. Offer help when you can, share relevant resources, and provide constructive feedback on others’ work.

通过分享你独特的视角和积极参与，有意识地投入你的社区。写下你解决过的问题，在 GitHub 或 Stack Overflow 上参与讨论，在会议上提出有思考深度的问题。把你的解决方案记录下来：下次再遇到同样的问题时，你会感谢自己。做一个被动的旁观者是不够的。力所能及的时候提供帮助，分享相关资源，对他人的工作给出建设性反馈。

Reach out to people periodically just to see how they’re doing and check in on what they’re working on. If people hear from you only when you need something, they will pick up on that and may start avoiding you.

定期联系别人，问问他们近况如何、在做什么。如果别人只在你需要什么时才收到你的消息，他们会察觉到这一点，并可能开始躲着你。

It may seem overly mechanical, but don’t be afraid to set periodic reminders to yourself to touch base. Schedule a recurring coffee meeting or lunch. If you find an article or podcast you think someone would appreciate, send it to them. Nurturing your network is time well spent.

这看起来也许过于机械，但别怕给自己设定期提醒来保持联系。安排一个定期的咖啡或午饭之约。如果你看到一篇文章或播客觉得某人会喜欢，就发给他。经营人脉是花得值的时间。

When you focus on these core principles while actively engaging with your communities and maintaining your relationships over time, you’ll build a professional network that supports your entire career journey.

当你专注于这些核心原则、积极参与社区并长期维持关系时，你就会建起一个支撑你整个职业旅程的职业人脉网。

Choose Quality, Not Quantity
重质量，而非数量

This is probably easier said than done, but you should avoid worrying about how many followers you have on a given social media platform. Instead, focus on cultivating the followers you do have by engaging with them and fostering real connections. Having 5,000 LinkedIn connections doesn’t mean anything if none of them will recommend you for a position. Focus on building meaningful relationships instead of the vanity metrics that seem to mean something in our society.
这大概说起来容易做起来难，但你应该别再操心自己在某个社交平台上有多少粉丝。相反，专注于经营你已有的粉丝，和他们互动、培养真实的关系。LinkedIn 上有 5000 个联系人，却没有一个人会推荐你去某个职位，那毫无意义。专注于建立有意义的关系，而不是那些在我们社会里似乎很重要的虚荣指标。

Interviewing isn’t just about landing your next job; it’s a fundamental skill that will pay dividends throughout your career. Whether you’re looking for an internal promotion, exploring new opportunities outside of your company, or trying to land

面试不只是为了拿下下一份工作；它是一项会在整个职业生涯中带来回报的基础技能。无论你是想争取内部晋升、在公司外部寻找新机会，还是试图拿到

your first job, mastering the art of interviewing is important for career growth in the field of software engineering.

（接上页）你的第一份工作，精通面试这门艺术对软件工程领域的职业成长都很重要。

The professional network that you’ve been cultivating plays an important role too. Your connections can provide helpful knowledge about companies, make introductions, and even serve as references.

你一直在经营的职业人脉也扮演着重要角色。你的关系能提供关于公司的有用信息、帮你内推，甚至当你的推荐人。

Even if you’re content in your current role, maintaining sharp interviewing skills will prepare you for unexpected opportunities, internal promotions, or something all too common in our industry: layoffs.

即使你对当前岗位很满意，保持敏锐的面试技能也会让你为意外机会、内部晋升，或我们这个行业再常见不过的事情——裁员——做好准备。

In the following sections, you’ll explore how to prepare for an interview, navigate the interview itself, and follow up professionally. These skills, like any other in software engineering, improve with practice and preparation.

在接下来的几节里，你将探索如何准备面试、如何应对面试本身，以及如何专业地跟进。这些技能和软件工程中任何其他技能一样，靠练习和准备而精进。

Interview preparation

This section explores preparation strategies that will help you stand out from other candidates and approach interviews with confidence. From leveraging research tools and your professional network to practicing common questions and honing your soft skills, you will learn how to showcase your technical expertise and professional value effectively. Remember that preparation is not just about technical knowledge; it is about presenting yourself as a well-rounded professional who can contribute meaningfully to an organization’s success.

本节探讨一些准备策略，帮你在其他候选人中脱颖而出、带着自信走进面试。从利用研究工具和职业人脉，到练习常见问题、打磨软技能，你将学到如何有效展示技术专长和职业价值。记住，准备不只是技术知识；它关乎把自己呈现为一个能为组织成功做出有意义贡献的、全面发展的专业人士。

Strategic research. Before applying to any position, thoroughly research both the company and the specific role to determine whether they align with your career goals and values. This initial research will help you determine what positions are a good fit. After you have secured an interview, deepen your research to understand the company’s culture, technical stack, business challenges, and interview process. Just by spending a little time doing this research, you have set yourself apart from other candidates who are probably submitting their 100th resume of the day.

战略性调研。在申请任何职位之前，彻底调研公司和具体岗位，判断它们是否与你的职业目标和价值观一致。这个初步调研会帮你确定哪些职位适合。拿到面试后，深入调研以了解公司文化、技术栈、业务挑战和面试流程。仅仅花一点时间做这些调研，你就已经把自己和那些大概今天已经投了第 100 份简历的候选人区分开来了。

Many resources are at your disposal for research, and it’s your job to use them to get the results you’re looking for. If you’re not already on LinkedIn, you should join, as it gives you another tool to build your professional network. It also provides insights into your interviewers, company background, and work culture.4 Your network can also provide invaluable insider perspectives about the interview process and company dynamics and even helpful information about your interviewers.

有许多资源可供你调研使用，你的工作就是用好它们得到你想要的结果。如果你还没上 LinkedIn，应该加入，因为它给你又一个建立职业人脉的工具。它还能让你了解面试官、公司背景和工作文化。4你的人脉还能提供关于面试流程、公司动态的宝贵内部视角，甚至关于面试官的有用信息。

4 And you may discover a connection that can help you stand out from other candidates.
而且你可能会发现一段关系，帮你在其他候选人中脱颖而出。

When preparing for an interview, modern AI tools like LLMs and research assistants can provide comprehensive insights into companies that go far beyond what’s available in job postings. These tools can analyze recent company news, surface detailed

准备面试时，像 LLM 和研究助手这样的现代 AI 工具，能提供远超招聘启事所载的、关于公司的全面洞见。这些工具可以分析公司近期新闻、呈现关于其技术栈的详细

information about their technology stacks, reveal their market positioning and competitive landscape, and even identify trends in their hiring patterns and company culture. This deep research capability allows you to better understand potential employers and prepare more effectively for interviews. Here is an example prompt you can use with your favorite AI tool to generate some research for your upcoming interview:

（接上页）信息、揭示其市场定位和竞争格局，甚至识别其招聘模式和公司文化的趋势。这种深度调研能力让你更好地理解潜在雇主，更有效地准备面试。下面是一个提示词示例，你可以用它配合你喜欢的 AI 工具，为即将到来的面试生成一些调研：

I have an upcoming interview with [COMPANY NAME] for a [POSITION] role.
Please help me prepare by providing comprehensive research on
the following:

and highlight any points that would be particularly valuable
to mention during the interview.

AI Deep Research
AI 深度研究

Modern AI assistants like ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Anthropic’s Claude can perform “deep research” by synthesizing information across multiple online sources. These tools do more than return search results. They analyze company data from many sources including news sites, tech blogs, financial reports, and employee reviews. From this analysis, they deliver comprehensive insights about technology stacks, business strategies, and company culture. Leverage these capabilities by asking specific questions and using follow-up queries to drill down into relevant areas for your interview preparation.
现代 AI 助手，如 ChatGPT、Google Gemini 和 Anthropic 的 Claude，能通过综合多个在线来源的信息来执行“深度研究”。这些工具不只是返回搜索结果。它们分析来自新闻网站、技术博客、财务报告和员工评价等多来源的公司数据。基于这种分析，它们交付关于技术栈、业务战略和公司文化的全面洞见。利用这些能力，提出具体问题，并用后续追问深入探讨与你面试准备相关的领域。

While AI tools can help with research, you need to be careful not to overuse them or use them without validating their results. HR departments and recruiters can easily spot AI-generated cover letters and resumes. If you need assistance with spelling, grammar, and overall writing improvement, use AI tools carefully but do not blindly accept entire cover letters. This is your first impression, and you want it to sound authentic and highlight the unique qualities that make you who you are.

虽然 AI 工具能帮你做调研，但你要小心，别过度使用，也别不加验证就使用它们的结果。HR 部门和招聘人员很容易认出AI 生成的求职信和简历。如果你需要在拼写、语法和整体写作提升上获得帮助，可以谨慎使用 AI 工具，但不要盲目接受整封求职信。这是你的第一印象，你希望它听起来真诚，并突出成就你的那些独特品质。

Another effective research tool is determining the company’s interview style. This could be a mix of technical and soft skill questions, FAANG-style algorithmic challenges, or take-home coding projects.5 Understanding what type of interview you are walking into will help you be more prepared and give you the confidence you need to ace that next interview.

另一个有效的调研工具是弄清公司的面试风格。它可能是技术与软技能问题的混合、FAANG 式算法题，或带回家做的编程项目。5了解你将走进什么样的面试，会帮你准备得更充分，给你拿下下次面试所需的信心。

FAANG 指 Facebook（现 Meta）、Amazon、Apple、Netflix 和 Google（现 Alphabet）。

Finally, you might need to get your boots on the ground and do some manual research. This could involve talking to people who are currently working there or who have worked there in the past.

最后，你可能需要亲自下场做一些手动调研。这可能包括和现在在那里工作、或曾经在那里工作过的人聊聊。

Being prepared can help put you at ease and give you confidence as you work your way through what is often a stressful interview process. Knowing what to expect means you won’t be caught off guard. Bringing your research into the interview process shows your potential new employer that you are engaged and serious about the opportunity, which can be the difference in getting an offer or not and may also result in a better compensation package.

充分准备能帮你放松下来，在走完通常压力不小的面试流程时给你信心。知道会发生什么，意味着你不会被打个措手不及。把你的调研带进面试流程，向潜在新雇主表明你投入其中、对这个机会是认真的；这可能就是拿到 offer 与否的差别，还可能带来更好的薪酬包。

Evaluating mutual fit. Your research shouldn’t just help you answer the interview questions; it can also be used to determine the questions you ask your interviewers. Remember that you’re interviewing them just as much as they’re interviewing you. Use your research to prepare questions that demonstrate your genuine interest while also helping you determine whether this opportunity aligns with your career goals. For example, ask about the following:

评估双方匹配度。你的调研不应只帮你回答面试问题；它还可以用来决定你向面试官提什么问题。记住，你在面试他们，正如他们在面试你。用你的调研准备一些问题，既展示你真诚的兴趣，又帮你判断这个机会是否与你的职业目标一致。例如，可以问以下这些：

  • Team dynamics and culture团队动态和文化
  • Technical challenges and decision-making processes技术挑战和决策流程
  • Tech stacks and development practices技术栈和开发实践
  • Growth and mentorship opportunities成长和指导机会
  • Travel requirements and percentage of time on the road出差要求和出差时间占比

Handling common questions. You will never be prepared to answer every question that an interviewer throws at you, but you can prepare yourself for some common questions that will come up in a lot of interviews. The first one you should be prepared

应对常见问题。你永远无法准备好回答面试官抛给你的每一个问题，但你可以为很多面试都会出现的一些常见问题做准备。第一个你应准备好的

for is “Why are you leaving your current position?” In this case, it’s important to be honest but also professional. It’s acceptable to respond with the following:

（接上页）问题是：“你为什么要离开现在的岗位？”这时，诚实但专业很重要。可以这样回答：

  • Seeking better compensation寻求更好的薪酬
  • Looking for new technical challenges寻找新的技术挑战
  • Pursuing growth opportunities追求成长机会

Avoid speaking negatively about your current employer, as it reflects poorly on your professionalism and interviewers will take note. Remember that professional networks are interconnected, and even with anonymized details, your references may be recognizable to others.5

避免说现雇主的坏话，因为这会显得你职业素养不够，面试官会注意到。记住，职业人脉是相互关联的；即使细节匿名，你的推荐人也可能被别人认出来。5

Another common question you will need to prepare for is “Where do you see yourself in N years?”6 This question helps employers evaluate your ambition, commitment, and whether your career goals align with their company’s direction. They want to understand whether you’re dedicated to professional development in both technical skills and leadership.

另一个你需要准备的常见问题是：“你认为自己 N 年后会在哪里？”6这个问题帮雇主评估你的抱负、投入度，以及你的职业目标是否与公司方向一致。他们想了解你是否致力于在技术技能和领导力两方面都进行职业发展。

6 “Where do you see me in N years?” is also an excellent question to ask your interviewer: they now imagine you are hired and progressing in your career with this organization.
“你认为我 N 年后会在哪里？”也是问面试官的绝佳问题：这样他们就会想象你已被录用、并在这家组织里职业发展的样子。

When answering, focus on your plans for professional growth and making an impact in the organization. You might discuss aspirations toward technical leadership, architecture roles, or mentoring others while keeping your goals realistic and aligned with typical career progression. 回答时，聚焦于你职业成长的计划和在组织中创造影响。你可以谈对技术领导、架构岗位或指导他人的向往，同时让目标现实、符合典型的职业晋升路径。这是引用你在本章前面讨论过的职业路线图的绝佳机会。

Technical questions software engineers should expect. Beyond general interview questions, software engineering roles will include technical questions that help a potential employer understand your approach to problem-solving and experience. Here are some common questions that you can prepare for:

软件工程师应预料到的技术问题。除了一般性面试问题，软件工程师岗位还会有技术问题，帮潜在雇主了解你的解决问题方式和经验。以下是一些你可以准备的常见问题：

“Walk me through how you would approach debugging a performance issue in production”

This tests your systematic thinking and understanding of debugging methodologies. Practice explaining your step-by-step process, from identifying symptoms to implementing solutions.

这考察你的系统思维和对调试方法论的理解。练习一步步讲清你的流程，从识别症状到实施解决方案。

“Describe a challenging technical problem you solved and your thought process”

Focus on your reasoning process, not just the final solution.

聚焦于你的推理过程，而不只是最终方案。

“How do you stay current with new technologies and decide what to learn?”

Demonstrate that you’re proactive about professional development. Mention specific resources you use and how you evaluate new tools or frameworks.

展示你在职业发展上是主动的。提到你用的具体资源，以及你如何评估新工具或框架。

原书第 354 页

“How do you approach code reviews and giving/receiving feedback?”

Shows your collaboration skills and commitment to code quality. Discuss both the technical and interpersonal aspects of effective code reviews.

展示你的协作能力和对代码质量的投入。讨论高效代码评审的技术和人际两个方面。

“Explain how you would design a simple system like a URL shortener or chat application”

This tests your ability to think through system architecture, data modeling, and scalability considerations. Start with basic requirements, then walk through your design decisions and potential trade-offs.

这考察你思考系统架构、数据建模和可扩展性考量的能力。从基本需求开始，然后讲清你的设计决策和潜在取舍。

Use Your Wins
用好你的成就清单

Remember those wins you have been tracking? They are about to become a tool you can lean into. Those technical problems you solved, the bugs you squashed, and those projects you delivered ahead of schedule are accomplishments that are yearning to be told. Make sure you find a way to review those wins and incorporate them into your conversations.
记得你一直在记录的那些成就吗？它们马上就要变成你可以倚仗的工具了。你解决过的那些技术难题、你捏死的那些 bug、你提前交付的那些项目，都是渴望被讲出来的成就。务必想办法回顾这些成就，并把它们融入你的谈话中。

Practice makes perfect. Preparation is a crucial step on your path to acing that next interview, with mock interviews serving as one the most effective tools at your disposal. This is much more than simply rehearsing answers: these practice sessions create a foundation that helps you enter the real interview with confidence, poise, and clarity of thought. Regular practice interviews transform potentially stressful encounters into familiar territory, allowing your authentic professional self to shine through when it matters most.

熟能生巧。准备是你拿下下次面试之路上关键的一步，而模拟面试是你可以使用的最有效工具之一。这远不止是排练答案：这些练习会话打下基础，帮你带着自信、沉着和清晰的思路走进真实面试。定期的模拟面试把可能充满压力的遭遇变成熟悉的领地，让你真实的职业自我在最关键的时刻闪耀出来。

To get the most out of your practice sessions, carefully select partners who can provide meaningful feedback. You’re not looking for a yes person or “That was great”; you want tangible feedback from someone who has been on that side of the interview before. If you can’t find a friend or coworker who fits that bill, try reaching out to someone in your professional network who might be willing to help out. There are also online platforms that specialize in technical interviews, such as interviewing.io, that offer structured practice opportunities with experienced professionals. Those local or online tech communities that you just learned about might also be a good resource to find suitable practice partners.

为了从练习中收获最多，仔细挑选能提供有意义反馈的搭档。你要的不是一个“好好先生”或只会说“挺好的”的人；你要的是一个曾经站在面试官那一侧的人给出的切实反馈。如果你找不到符合条件的朋友或同事，试着联系你职业人脉里可能愿意帮忙的人。还有一些专注于技术面试的在线平台，比如 interviewing.io，提供与有经验的专业人士进行结构化练习的机会。你刚了解到的那些本地或在线技术社区，也可能是找到合适练习搭档的好资源。

To get the most out of each practice session, you need to approach it with the same seriousness you would bring to an actual interview:

By incorporating regular, structured practice into your interview preparation strategy, you transform the interview process from an intimidating obstacle into a well-rehearsed opportunity to showcase your qualifications and potential. Now that you are prepared for that upcoming interview, let’s discuss some practical tips you can use during the actual interview.

通过把定期、结构化的练习纳入面试准备策略，你把面试流程从一个令人生畏的障碍，变成了一个排练充分、展示你资历和潜力的机会。既然你已为即将到来的面试做好准备，我们来谈谈在真实面试中可以用的一些实用技巧。

During the interview

This section prepares you for the crucial moments when you’re face-to-face with your interviewers. You’ll learn some practical strategies for commanding technical conversations, demonstrating problem-solving skills beyond just syntax, and presenting yourself professionally, whether in-person or virtually.

本节为你与面试官面对面的关键时刻做准备。你将学到一些实用策略：主导技术对话、展示超越语法本身的解决问题能力，以及无论线下面试还是线上面试都专业地呈现自己。

Command the technical interview. Remember that you have prepared for this interview, so enter with confidence and the mindset that you are going to ace it. When presented with coding challenges it’s important to resist the urge to immediately start typing or writing on the whiteboard. Instead, try to think through and verbalize your thought process. This is a key skill that the person interviewing you is looking for more often than the semantics of writing code, which we assume you know how to do. Begin by clarifying requirements and constraints, then outline your approach before implementing a solution.

主导技术面试。记住，你已经为这次面试做了准备，所以带着自信和“我要拿下它”的心态进场。面对编程挑战时，重要的是忍住立刻开始在白板上敲字或写字的冲动。相反，试着想清楚并口述你的思考过程。面试官要找的关键技能往往正是这个，而不是写代码的语法——我们假设你已经会写代码。先澄清需求和约束，再概述你的方法，然后才实现方案。

When solving an unfamiliar problem, show your value through a clear approach: break the problem into smaller parts, think about different solutions, and explain

解决一个不熟悉的问题时，通过清晰的方法展示你的价值：把问题拆成小块，思考不同方案，并解释

your chosen path. Use your documented technical wins as examples to show your expertise when talking about past projects and how they might relate to this problem.

（接上页）你选择的路径。在谈论过去项目及其与当前问题的关联时，用你记录的技术成就作为例子来展示专长。

Be professional. Beyond your technical prowess, professionalism can have a huge impact on your interview. The following are some practical insights on how to present yourself effectively in an in-person or virtual interview.

保持专业。除了技术实力，专业素养对你的面试也有巨大影响。以下是一些实用见解，关于如何在线下或线上面试中有效呈现自己。

The following are some general steps you can take to prepare for your interview:

以下是你为面试做准备可以采取的一些一般步骤：

  • Research your interviewers’ names and roles. This shows attention to detail and helps you address them personally.查清面试官的姓名和职位。这体现你注重细节，也帮你以姓氏称呼他们。
  • Prepare thoughtful questions about aspects of the role not covered in the job description.准备一些有思考深度的问题，关于职位描述里没提到的方面。
  • Bring multiple copies of your resume, even for virtual interviews (you can reference it during the conversation).带上多份简历复印件，即使是线上面试（谈话中你可以参考它）。
  • Dress for success. This goes for in-person or virtual interviews.为成功着装。线下面试和线上面试都适用。
  • Get a good night’s sleep before.前一晚睡个好觉。
  • Silence your device notifications.把设备通知静音。

When it comes to in-person interviews, make sure to arrive early to account for unexpected delays, giving yourself time to mentally prepare. This might seem obvious, but arriving late or rushing to get there can negatively affect your mindset and performance.

线下面试时，务必早点到，以应对意外延误，给自己留出心理准备的时间。这也许显而易见，但迟到或一路狂奔赶到会负面影响你的心态和表现。

For virtual interviews, all the general interviewing tips apply, but with additional technical considerations. The following are tips for preparing your environment:

线上面试时，所有一般面试技巧都适用，但还有额外的技术考量。以下是准备环境的技巧：

  • Test your technology. Make sure your camera, microphone, and lighting are all ready to go. Also test your virtual meeting application to make sure you can log in at the scheduled interview time.测试你的技术设备。确保摄像头、麦克风和灯光都就绪。还要测试你的虚拟会议应用，确保你能在预定面试时间登录。
  • Silence all application notifications.把所有应用通知静音。
  • Close unnecessary applications that might slow down your system during live coding exercises.关掉不必要的应用，以免在实时编程练习时拖慢系统。
  • Make sure the background you display on camera is clean and tidy.确保镜头里的背景干净整洁。
  • Let household members know you need uninterrupted time.告诉家里人你需要不被打扰的时间。

Embrace the experience. The interview experience is all about finding the right match, for both sides. There is a chance that you might not land that first interview or even the first three, and that is OK. Treat each interview as an opportunity to build experience and professional connections. If you make a lasting impression, future

拥抱这段经历。面试经历的核心是为双方找到合适的匹配。你有可能第一次面试没成，甚至前三次都没成，这没关系。把每次面试都当作积累经验和职业关系的机会。如果你留下了持久的印象，未来的

opportunities could arise from this experience. Show genuine enthusiasm for the opportunity and the company.

（接上页）机会可能会从这段经历中浮现。对这个机会和这家公司展现真诚的热情。

After the interview

The interview is over, you’ve done your best, and now begins the waiting game. The good news is, there are usually only two possible outcomes: you either get an offer or you don’t. If you receive an offer, congratulations! It’s time to evaluate the opportunity, negotiate your compensation package, and prepare for your first day. However, not every interview leads to a job offer, and that’s perfectly normal in the journey of a software engineer.

面试结束了，你已尽力，现在等待的游戏开始了。好消息是，通常只有两种可能的结果：你拿到 offer，或者没拿到。如果拿到了 offer，恭喜！是时候评估这个机会、谈你的薪酬包，并为第一天做准备了。然而，并非每次面试都会带来录用，这在软件工程师的旅程中完全正常。

The following sections focus on handling those situations where you don’t get the position, not because they’re more common, but because they present valuable growth opportunities that are often overlooked.

接下来几节专注于处理你没拿到职位的情况，不是因为它们更常见，而是因为它们提供了常常被忽视的宝贵成长机会。

Learning from the experience. As with dating, you will need to accept the reality that not all interviews will go well, and you will face rejections. Most of the time job rejections have little to do with your capabilities. Companies might have decided to go with an internal candidate, change priorities, hit a hiring freeze, or simply find a closer skill match to what they are looking for. The key here is you can’t take it personally.

从经历中学习。就像约会一样，你需要接受这个现实：不是所有面试都会顺利，你会面对拒绝。大多数时候，求职拒绝和你的能力关系不大。公司可能决定用内部候选人、改变优先级、冻结招聘，或只是找到了更贴合他们需求的技能匹配者。这里的关键是：你不能把它往心里去。

Growing from feedback. If you didn’t get the job, you could hang your head and deliberate internally on why the interviewers didn’t want you, or you could use this as another chance to grow. This is a perfect opportunity to request feedback about their decision. This information can be extremely valuable for your professional development. If they have identified areas for improvement, use this as insight and motivation to focus your learning, and give yourself a better chance in the next one. Because there will be a next one!

从反馈中成长。如果你没得到这份工作，你可以垂头丧气、暗自琢磨面试官为什么不想要你，也可以把这当作又一次成长的机会。这是请求对方就其决定给出反馈的绝佳机会。这些信息对你的职业发展可能极其宝贵。如果他们指出了需要改进的地方，把它作为洞见和动力来聚焦你的学习，让自己在下一次机会里更有胜算。因为还会有下一次！

Again, you never know what can happen. Another position might open up that might be a better fit or a more interesting opportunity. They might be able to connect you to a friend of theirs who’s hiring at a different company. Heck, they might move to a new organization and recommend you to a hiring manager. The point is simple: don’t burn bridges.

再说一遍，你永远不知道会发生什么。可能会有另一个更匹配、或更有趣的职位开放。他们也许能把你介绍给在另一家公司招人的朋友。嗨，他们可能跳到新组织，然后把你推荐给一位招聘经理。要点很简单：别把桥烧了。

Create Work–Life Balance

Being a software engineer can consume your entire life if you let it. Between the constant pressure to learn the latest technologies, tackle increasingly complex problems, and meet (sometimes unrealistic) project deadlines, the boundaries between work and personal life can easily blur.

如果你放任不管，做软件工程师会吞噬你的整个人生。在不断学习最新技术、应对日益复杂的问题、以及赶上（有时不切实际的）项目截止日期的持续压力之间，工作与个人生活的界限很容易模糊。

Understanding the challenges of software development

Every profession brings its own set of unique challenges, and software development is no different. If you can first identify these challenges, you will be able to look out for them and be ready to deal with them. The following are some common challenges and how to deal with them:

每个职业都有其独特的挑战，软件开发也不例外。如果你能先识别出这些挑战，就能留意它们、准备好应对。以下是一些常见挑战以及应对方法：

Keeping up with rapid technological change

One of the biggest challenges you will face is the pace at which technology changes. This requires constant learning and adaptation to stay current with tools, frameworks, and languages.

你将面对的最大挑战之一，就是技术变化的速度。这要求你不断学习和适应，以跟上工具、框架和语言的最新进展。

How to deal with it:

如何应对：

Continuous learning

  • You learned a lot about this in Chapter 12, but you need to be deliberate about what you’re learning and continue your education through books, courses, workshops, and conferences to stay updated.你在第 12 章学过很多这方面的内容，但你需要有意识地选择学什么，并通过书籍、课程、工作坊和大会继续学习，以保持更新。

Tech radar

  • As you learned earlier in this chapter, a tech radar is a useful tool for deciding what to learn next and aligning those options with your career goals.正如你在本章前面学到的，技术雷达是一个有用的工具，帮你决定接下来学什么，并让这些选择与你的职业目标对齐。

Networking

  • Collaborating with coworkers and friends to share knowledge and stay up-to-date with industry trends.与同事和朋友协作，分享知识，跟上行业趋势。

Problems that are mentally engaging are hard to “turn off”

When you work on mentally challenging problems, it can be difficult to walk away from the problem, which can quickly take over your personal life.

当你从事需要动脑的挑战性问题时，很难从问题中抽离，它会迅速占据你的个人生活。

How to deal with it:

如何应对：

Step away

  • Some of your best solutions will come to you when you step away from the keyboard and let your subconscious work on the problem. Go for a walk or a run and let your mind wander.当你离开键盘、让潜意识去琢磨问题时，一些最好的解决方案会冒出来。去散散步或跑跑步，让思绪漫游。

Rubber ducking

  • Sometimes talking the whole problem out to someone else (or some inanimate object like a rubber duck or AI chatbot) can provide gaps in your logic or help you understand the issue more clearly.有时把整个问题讲给别人听（或讲给橡皮鸭、AI 聊天机器人之类无生命物体），能暴露你逻辑中的漏洞，或帮你更清楚地理解问题。
